overall: As of 12:50 ET, New York City is sitting at a running max of 80.1°F with a still-positive velocity of +4.1°F/hr, suggesting modest additional warming potential remains. However, a Flood Watch is in effect and the NWS narrative calls for showers and thunderstorms this afternoon, which will likely cap convective heating well before the typical mid-afternoon peak. The very high dewpoint (72°F) confirms a deeply moist, increasingly unstable airmass — atmospheric conditions are more supportive of heavy rainfall than of sustained surface temperature rises.
forecast_obs_notes: There is stark disagreement between the NWP models (GFS 88.4°F, ECMWF 90.9°F, HRRR 91.7°F, NBM 88.1°F) and both the NWS text forecast (high near 83°F) and the META/intraday observation-driven models, which concentrate probability heavily in the 82-83°F bucket (62.3%) and 80-81°F bucket (31.2%). The NWP guidance appears inconsistent with the actual storm/cloud cover environment already developing, and the intraday model grounded in real-time ASOS observations is far more credible at this stage of the day.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely daily high is in the 82–83°F range, consistent with the NWS narrative forecast of 'near 83°F' and the META model's dominant 62.3% probability assigned to that even bucket. With the current temp already at 80.1°F and warming, there is a path to touching 83°F before convective activity shuts down surface heating — but surpassing it meaningfully is unlikely given the Flood Watch context and heavy afternoon storm threat. For the active even-bucket Kalshi market, the 82-83°F bucket is the clear highest-confidence position, with NWP-driven signals pointing to 86-87°F or higher appearing significantly overstated given observed conditions.
